verdicts.reason: Quotes verify. ticketing-box-office-index.md:49 literally reads '14 intra-domain pairs, 6 rejected pairs, 8 cross-cut mechanisms routed out'; the CX file actually enumerates CX-01..CX-21 (ticketing-box-office-cx.md:12-32), R-01..R-07 (:396-402) and 10 routed-out mechanism rows (:379-388). The stale '8' is repeated at index:91 (D-06) and index:100 (Q-02). Separately index:70 gives 19.12 'Operator | Config' against a legend that lists Config and Reports as distinct levels (index:55), while 19.12-ticket-delivery-fan-wallet.md:22 grants 'Operator | Config + Reports'. Real internal inconsistency, so upheld — but downgraded: the claimed forced invention is refuted, because the delivery-failure list is authored in full at 19.12:22 and the CX file itself is the enumeration authority. No implementer builds anything different from a stale count.

Quotes verify (19.01.02:34 identity, :46 enforcement, :72 auto-release exclusion, :96 happy-path carve-out, 19.01.05:25) but the inference does not. 19.01.05:106 D-01 excludes accessible inventory from the *hold* mechanism's auto-release ('the auto-release control is structurally absent'), not from being sellable: 19.01.05:29 puts accessible positions on the ordinary storefront at the ordinary time and 19.01.05:109 D-04 demands no proof of disability, so an unsold accessible position IS sellable-right-now and sits in `remaining` exactly as the six-term identity requires. The worked example is wrong on its own terms — remaining = 300 including the 4 accessible positions; the 296 figure is the general-inventory presentation, a different quantity. The 'Sold out (accessible)' and 'Conditional release' states (19.01.05:75-76) have a quantity to operate on because the block is a typed set of positions (19.01.05:25), and whether that set is modelled as a seventh column or a sub-partition of `remaining` is a data-model choice belonging to the architecture layer, not vision behaviour. No product behaviour must be invented.

Quotes verify verbatim, including the Q-01 text at 19.01.04-seating-model-ga-reserved-seat-maps.md:94 — but that is the refutation, not the finding. Q-01 explicitly names the defect ('so this file's assertion that "seat maps are a room asset (domain 16)" is wrong'), carries Owner 'Agent', and carries a live target in its Deferred-To cell ('seat-map ownership collision -> `16.01.02` Q-02'). The parent index tracks the identical residual at ticketing-box-office-index.md:110 and 19.01.05:118 records the mirror. This is a documented, owned, targeted collision — the documented mechanism, not a silent contradiction. The auditor's own mitigation also holds: 19.01.04:95 Q-02 tiers reserved/mixed to `could`, off the v1 path.

One of the five citations is fabricated: 19.01.05-accessible-seating-companion-tickets.md:21 is the Fan row of the Role Lens ('The only persona that transacts on it...') and contains no comp text; grepping the file for '19.02' returns only :61 and :97, so the claimed sentence at :21 does not exist anywhere. The other four verify (19.01.05:61, :97; 19.01.03:67, :104). But every one of them carries the correct title beside the wrong number — 'Touches **19.02 Comps & Guest Lists**' and 'Touches **19.03 On-sale / Checkout** and **19.05 Box Office (walk-up)**' — so a reader resolving by name lands on 19.03-guest-list-comps-index.md:1 and 19.02-on-sale-announce-presale-index.md:1 respectively. The behaviour asserted (the only zero-cost accessible ticket is a comp; the fee profile is owned here and consumed by the door/checkout surfaces) is unambiguous under every reading. Citation typos, not divergent builds.

All five markers verify (19.01-ticket-config-scaling-allocations-cx.md:31, :56, :64, :76, :84) and every one carries a named target — '`[PENDING — /ideate-discover Step 5 deepening]`' — which is the kit's documented deferral marker with the responsible stage named. The sixth citation, 19.01.04:54's '`[PENDING — Q-03, /write-be-spec]`', likewise carries both a question id and a stage. The staleness is real but consequence-free and the auditor concedes it: 'Nothing product-level for CX-01's concurrency question — 19.01.02:189 supplies the answer', and 19.01.04's Q-03 is resolved by an authored rule (19.01.02 D-13, edges-inward release) so no implementer is left inventing behaviour. Contrast the genuinely malformed bare markers upheld at #008/#017/#018, which name neither owner nor target.

Quotes verify (19.01.02:65, :68, :101, :155) but the reference frame is not actually ambiguous. The normative sentence at :68 is unqualified — 'The owner is prompted **7 days and 24 hours before** the deadline' — and the happy-path sentence at :101 self-corrects inside itself: 'At `doors − 7 days` and `doors − 24h` **relative to each hold's deadline**'. The States row at :155 uses bare '`−7d` / `−24h`' under the trigger 'A hold's deadline arrives', again deadline-relative. Three of three normative statements resolve to deadline-relative; the `doors −` prefix at :101 is loose notation contradicted by its own trailing clause. No competent implementer builds prompts that fire seven days after the release they are supposed to precede (DT-13, :181).

Every cited item verifies and every one is tracked. The four questions (19.02-on-sale-announce-presale-index.md:51, :52; 19.02.01-announce-on-sale-scheduling.md:127, :128) each carry Owner 'User' and a Deferred-To target, and each sits in a visible Open Questions table where the owner can still answer — the domain index demonstrates exactly this re-pointing at ticketing-box-office-index.md:103. The three CX markers (19.02-on-sale-announce-presale-cx.md:69, :73, :79) each name their stage. None is a bare marker. The auditor concedes the substance: 'Nothing behavioural'.

The core citation verifies and is genuinely malformed: 19.03-guest-list-comps-cx.md:61 reads '3. **Permission intersection**: The right to add a guest and the right to certify a statement should not sit with the same person unchecked. `[PENDING]`' — no owner, no stage, no question id, on the race the same file names at :54. That is the carve-out from the tracked-deferral rule. Downgraded from the finding's framing, though: the malicious case IS answered — 19.05.05-box-office-close-certified-statement.md:66 handles 'Operator freezes, then self-authorises comps to depress payable gross before certifying (malicious)' with the domain's attribution-not-prevention mechanism (author + timestamp + distinct line, never netted), and :63 scopes certification to Operator-Full. So no implementer must invent a check; what is missing is the owner on the marker. The MoSCoW half of the claim (19.03.02:148, :149) is refuted — both rows carry Owner 'User' and a target.

Quotes verify (19.04.04-door-age-id-verification.md:27, :35, :93, :115) but the answer is authored in the same file, in the row the finding itself quotes. Q-04 at :115 states the resolution outright: 'There is therefore no upstream default to inherit, and the restriction is **Operator-declared per show here**.' The two supposed inventions are both authored: the default is given by the States table at :65 ('Empty (unrestricted) | Show carries no age restriction | Plain accept verdict'), and with no inherited floor the 'adjustable upward' clause is simply superseded — the Operator declares the value. The Error row at :67 is about the scanner's *manifest replica* lacking the show's restriction data, not about a licence field. The parent index tracks the residual empirical legal work with an explicit target (ticketing-box-office-index.md:110, '-> `/create-prd-security`'). A resolved Open Question that directly supersedes stale Behavior prose is a marker, not a silent contradiction — the blocking severity does not survive.

All four citations verify verbatim: 19.04.03-multi-scanner-coordination-re-entry.md:27-30 offers three per-show re-entry policies including '**Re-entry via re-scan**'; :47 treats it as selectable ('Re-entry via re-scan policy chosen ... Warned at configuration'); D-01 at :89 states 'Re-entry is via physical token; the ticket remains **strictly use-once**'; and 19.04.01-ticket-scan-validation.md:72 lists 're-entry' as an amber accept-with-warning verdict, which only exists under re-scan. Two normative statements — a configurable three-way policy versus a strictly use-once ticket — cannot both hold, and neither carries a marker, a question id, or a deferral. Warning rather than blocking because the token path is fully authored and is the stated default (:35, 'for most club shows, re-entry via token'), so the door ships either way; what diverges is whether the re-scan option exists in configuration.

Citations verify (19.04-door-scanning-access-control-index.md:54 and 19.04.01-ticket-scan-validation.md:119, both Owner 'User' / Deferred-To 'MoSCoW'; 19.04-door-scanning-access-control-cx.md:73 '`[PENDING — /ideate-discover Step 5 deepening]`') and all three carry a target. More decisively, the finding's own evidence shows the question is alive and owned at the level that matters: ticketing-box-office-index.md:103 carries the identical question as Q-05 with Owner 'User' and Deferred-To '`/create-prd`', and records why MoSCoW did not settle it. A leaf row pointing at a spent gate while the parent holds the same question against a live gate is redundancy, not a lost decision. The auditor concedes 'Nothing behavioural — the door's own behaviour is fully authored either way'.

Both formulas verify verbatim and they genuinely differ. 19.05.01-live-count-manifest-state.md:36 defines 'Remaining | Sellable right now (= capacity − killed − held − paid − comp)' and its counter table at :27-36 has no `carted` row at all, while 19.01.02-capacity-manifest-allocations-holds.md:34 makes the enforced identity 'licensed capacity = killed + held + comp + paid + **carted** + remaining' with `carted` given its own writer (:43) and its own rule (:122, 'A hold draws only from unreserved `remaining` — never from `carted`'). 19.05.01:42 repeats the carted-free initialisation. Since 19.05.01 D-01 (:116) forbids consumers computing their own count, the storefront's availability boolean (D-04, :119) reads whichever definition ships. Downgraded from blocking because precedence is stated: 19.01.02:46 declares 'the manifest is the state, the live count is its reporting face', so an implementer has an authored tie-breaker and lands on the six-term identity. The defect is the omission of `carted` from the canonical reporting table, not an unresolvable fork.

All three citations verify (19.05.04-walk-up-day-of-show-sales.md:139, Owner 'User' / 'MoSCoW'; 19.05-box-office-counts-drops-cx.md:72 and :94, both '`[PENDING — /ideate-discover Step 5 deepening]`') and every one names a target. None is a bare marker. The auditor's own text refutes the substance twice over: 'Nothing behavioural — the draining/quiesce sequence is authored at 19.05.04 D-12 and 19.05.05 Behavior', and it concedes 'the marker is stale rather than open'. A stale stage pointer over already-authored behaviour is not an ambiguity an implementer can trip on.

The marker verifies at 19.06-refunds-cancellations-rescheduling-cx.md:45 — '**Synthesis questions answered**: `[PENDING]` — jurisdiction mapping required first (parent Q-01)' — and it names a target: parent Q-01, which is live and owned at 19.06-refunds-cancellations-rescheduling-index.md:46 ('**[OWNER]** **What is the refund policy?**', Owner 'User'). The stated precondition wording is stale (jurisdiction was settled US-only), but the chain still terminates on a tracked owner decision, not on nobody. The product consequence the finding worries about is authored regardless — the auditor concedes '19.06.03 D-02 and D-06 author the mandatory deadline and forbid an open-ended TBC', so an indefinite postponement already cannot be a resting state. Nothing is invented.

Both quotes verify (19.07.04-manual-count-entry-attestation.md:85 and D-08 at :124; 19.05.05-box-office-close-certified-statement.md:121 D-07 and the States row at :83) — and they say the same thing. 19.07.04:85 defines the lapse as 'Distinct from an active acceptance ... **never shown as an active accept**' and D-08 binds it 'never as an active acceptance'; 19.05.05:83 records 'silence as silence, not consent'. Both files model lapse as its own terminal state that is not consent. What differs is the label ('Accepted (lapsed)' versus 'lapsed'), and the enum member name is downstream detail belonging to the contract layer, not vision behaviour. The imagined implementer who 'will treat `accepted_lapsed` as accepted' has to ignore the prohibition printed in the same table row. The state machines also legitimately differ in size (19.07.04 adds Revised, Reconstructed, Unknown), so a terminal-value count is not a like-for-like comparison.

Citations verify (19.07-external-ticketing-integration-index.md:53, :54 and 19.07.03-count-discrepancy-reconciliation.md:107, all Owner 'User' / 'MoSCoW'; 19.07-external-ticketing-integration-cx.md:53 and :59, both naming Step 5) and each carries a target. Q-03 in particular is the same question the parent domain index holds as Q-05 with Owner 'User' and Deferred-To '`/create-prd`' (ticketing-box-office-index.md:103), so the hinge decision is owned against a live gate — the leaf row is a duplicate pointer, not the only record. The auditor concedes 'Nothing behavioural'.

Verified verbatim: 19.08.02-meet-and-greet-scheduling.md:49 still reads 'Order of refund is a fairness question — `[PENDING]`' with no owner, no stage and no question id, while the same file's Q-02 at :102 resolves precisely that ordering ('**RESOLVED — the domain's ratified capacity-reduction ladder applies**', 19.01.02 D-12: volunteers, then reverse-chronological). A bare marker with neither owner nor target is malformed tracking by definition, and here it also advertises as open a question the file itself closed. Warning, not blocking: the authored ladder is unambiguous, so a spec writer who reads the Open Questions table builds the right thing; the row's residual 'the artist's call stands' reads naturally as the capacity cut standing, not as refund-order discretion.

Both markers verify verbatim and both are bare: 19.09.02-ticket-transfer-delivery-controls.md:58 'Transfer of an accessible ticket | The accessible position may not suit the recipient | `[PENDING]`' and 19.09.03-resale-price-caps-face-value-exchange.md:53 'Buyer pays; the transfer fails | Money moved, ticket did not | **Must be atomic. `[PENDING]`**' — neither names an owner, a stage, or a question id. The coverage claim also checks out: 19.09.02's Q-01..Q-04 and 19.01.05's Q-01..Q-04 do not reach accessible-ticket transfer, and 19.01.05:57/:109 foreclose the obvious mitigations. Accessible transfer is a genuine unowned product policy (permit / block / permit-with-disclosure, and whether the companion entitlement at 19.01.05:27 travels). Warning rather than blocking because the second half is weaker — 'Must be atomic' states the product-level requirement, and the compensating-action mechanics are transaction semantics for the architecture layer (cf. 19.06.01:135 D-08's all-or-nothing exchange).

All three stale citations verify verbatim — 19.09.02-ticket-transfer-delivery-controls.md:55 ('19.06.01 Q-03; a genuine tangle'), :91 ('refunding a transferred ticket splits payer from holder (19.06.01 Q-03)') and 19.09-ticketing-fraud-bot-resale-controls-cx.md:54 — and so does the resolution: 19.06.01-individual-refunds-exchanges.md:137 D-10 authors holder-requests / payer-is-paid / holder-must-acknowledge and states '**resolves prior Q-03**', while that file's Q-03 at :145 is now the unrelated externally-ticketed brokering question. Three normative references present a decided rule as open and point at a renumbered target. Warning, not blocking: a reader who follows the reference into 19.06.01 meets D-10 and the explicit edge-case row at :55 covering payer-not-equal-holder, so nothing is invented — the defect is that transfer's owning feature advertises settled behaviour as unwritten.
